title: Find missing invoice numbers
summary: Auditors want every gap in the invoice number sequence, as ranges.
prompt: Invoice numbers must be continuous; the auditor wants every gap. Return one row per gap with
`gap_start` (first missing number), `gap_end` (last missing number) and `missing` (how many),
ordered by `gap_start`. Only gaps **between** the lowest and highest issued number count.
A number can appear twice (re-issued invoices); that is not a gap.
setup: CREATE TABLE invoices (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, number INTEGER NOT NULL, issued_on TEXT NOT NULL);
solution: SELECT number, LEAD(number) OVER (ORDER BY number) AS next_number
SELECT number + 1 AS gap_start, next_number - 1 AS gap_end, next_number - number - 1 AS missing
wrong: SELECT number, LEAD(number) OVER (ORDER BY number) AS next_number FROM invoices
SELECT number + 1 AS gap_start, next_number AS gap_end, next_number - number AS missing
SELECT number + 1 AS gap_start, number + 1 AS gap_end, 1 AS missing
WHERE number + 1 NOT IN (SELECT number FROM invoices)
hints: `LEAD(number) OVER (ORDER BY number)` puts the next issued number on the same row.
Where the next number is more than 1 higher, everything strictly between them is missing.
The gap runs from `number + 1` to `next_number - 1`; filter with `WHERE` in an outer query, since window results cannot be filtered in the same SELECT.
